paras: The threatened lynching of James Stockton took place near Broad Ripple, Indiana, in August 1895, when an armed mob chased and captured Stockton, a Black man accused of firing at a farmer's grandson. According to a wire report, older citizens kept the crowd from lynching him only with difficulty; he was arrested and charged with the shooting.
Barney Cline, Ernest Cline's grandfather, was described as a wealthy farmer of Washington township. Stockton was described as "colored" and as recently arrived from Kentucky.

The Indianapolis Journal reported that on Monday night [August 5] Ernest Cline, who lived with his father near Broad Ripple, was fired at from a stall when he entered the family barn. The shot missed, but the powder burned his face; the wire version said buckshot carried away his hat after he followed a strange dog into the barn.

In the wire account the assailant escaped, and the aroused neighborhood formed "a mob of men and boys, heavily armed and re-enforced by dogs," which chased him all night. The man captured near Broad Ripple proved to be Stockton, and "the older citizens had difficulty in preventing a lynching." The Journal said only that Cline recognized his assailant and that Stockton was arrested on Tuesday.
The Cline family could not account for the attack, and Stockton was said to offer no explanation. No report of a hearing, trial or outcome for Stockton appears in the coverage.

The Indianapolis Journal gave the case four sentences, headed "Fired at from a Stall," in its City News Notes of August 7, without mentioning a mob. Two days later the Scranton Tribune ran a front-page wire dispatch headed "Assassin Run to Earth," calling Stockton "the would-be assassin" and "the negro" and reporting the near-lynching without comment.

The reports differ on dates: the Journal placed the shooting on Monday night and the arrest on Tuesday, while the wire dispatch dated August 8 put the shooting a day earlier and the capture that afternoon. The local Journal printed its account on August 7, before the wire's dates, so its timing is the better evidence.

reader.title: Threatened lynching of James Stockton
bases: An armed mob pursued and captured James Stockton, accused of shooting at a farmer's grandson, and older citizens had difficulty preventing a lynching; no one was killed (A2; the shooting and arrest also in A1).

Stockton was not killed; the wire story says a mob of men and boys chased and captured him and was kept from lynching him only with difficulty, making this a threatened lynching rather than a lynching (A2).

The shooting at Ernest Cline and Stockton's arrest appear in two independent reports (A1, A2), but the mob chase and the lynching threat appear only in the wire story (A2); the local Indianapolis Journal brief does not mention a mob (A1).

accounts.label: Indianapolis Journal local brief
accounts.gist: Cline was fired at from a stall in his father's barn on Monday night, recognized his assailant, and Stockton was arrested on Tuesday; no pursuit or mob is mentioned.

accounts.label: Wire report (Indianapolis, Aug. 8)
accounts.gist: Cline followed a strange dog into his grandfather's barn and was fired on; the assailant escaped, an armed mob with dogs chased him all night, and when Stockton was captured near Broad Ripple older citizens had difficulty preventing a lynching.

framing.detail: The Indianapolis Journal ran four sentences under 'Fired at from a Stall' among its City News Notes, describing an arrest without comment.
The Scranton Tribune's front-page wire story, headed 'Assassin Run to Earth', calls Stockton 'the would-be assassin' and 'the negro' and reports the near-lynching without comment.

versions.value: Shooting 'yesterday' [Aug. 7] and capture 'this afternoon' [Aug. 8], dispatch dated Aug. 8

conflicts.note: The Indianapolis Journal is local and was printed on Aug. 7, before the dates the wire gives, so its Aug. 5-6 dating is the better evidence; the wire's relative dates appear to have been carried over from an earlier text.

versions.value: Cline recognized his assailant and Stockton was arrested
The assailant escaped and was captured by a pursuing mob after an all-night chase

conflicts.note: The two are not strictly exclusive, but the local brief mentions no mob or pursuit.

versions.value: The shot did not hit Cline; powder burned his face
Buckshot carried away his hat; face badly burned by the powder flash

conflicts.note: Minor difference; both agree he was not wounded by shot.

record_check.dossier: The local Journal of Aug. 7 places the shooting Monday night [Aug. 5] and the arrest Tuesday [Aug. 6]; the wire's Aug. 7-8 dating is later and less reliable
Pursuit and capture by the mob, and a threatened lynching; the shooting was the act Stockton was accused of, not an act of the mob
Threatened: the mob captured him and older citizens prevented a lynching with difficulty; no act toward killing him is described
In pursuit: the mob chased and captured him; he was then arrested
